A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScanSSC study, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The complete v1 contains no appendix; v2 adds supplementary Sections A–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanSSC results on SemanticKITTI and SSCBench-KITTI-360, together with component, direction, and masking ablations in Tables 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds computational measurements, controlled ablations, and evaluations of selected challenging scenes in the supplement.

M1.justification: The viewing transformation, axis-specific Scan Module, feature fusion, Scan Loss, and overall training objective remain unchanged. Appendices B and G provide implementation details and pseudocode without establishing an actual method revision.

E1.justification: The two benchmark datasets and SSC task are retained. Appendix E adds targeted evaluation of non-axis-aligned curved-road and shadowed scenes, alongside dedicated heavily occluded cases, modestly extending the tested environmental conditions.

E2.justification: Published-method comparators in Tables 3–4 remain unchanged. Tables D.1–D.2 add local comparison methods: concatenation followed by linear projection, averaging, learned weighted-sum fusion, and spatially reweighted or scalar-weighted cross-entropy.

E3.justification: New evaluation procedures include single-sample timing on one A6000 GPU, class-group scoring over distant half-regions, manually selected scene-condition subsets, and loss controls including a cross-entropy coefficient of 10. The training settings and dataset splits newly documented in A–B do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices D–F substantially expand validation with fusion alternatives, Scan Loss coefficient sensitivity, cross-entropy reweighting controls, subsidiary-component ablations, and single-axis visual comparisons. They also add distant-region class-group analysis, curved-road and shadow/occlusion evaluations, and further qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional tables and sensitivity plot retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Main-text numerical results remain unchanged, but the supplement adds substantial new findings. Table D.2 reports 17.12 mIoU for ScanSSC versus 16.50 and 16.74 for loss controls; Appendix E reports curved-road mIoU of 14.56 versus CGFormer's 13.77. Computational costs, group-wise scores, and further qualitative outcomes are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation is retained. Equation 6 replaces an index over three features with explicit axis labels, expressing the same weighted sum. No new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same distance-dependent completion problem, Scan Module/Scan Loss contributions, synergy claim, and state-of-the-art claims with identical headline benchmark scores.

C2.justification: The supplement adds explanations concerning excessive Scan Loss weighting and overfitting, complementary axis features, adaptive fusion, and contextual supervision beyond simple loss reweighting. It also discusses computational trade-offs and applicability to selected non-axis-aligned scenes, while retaining the main near-to-far interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B newly document dataset conventions, 25 training epochs, four A6000 GPUs, batch size four, AdamW settings, the learning-rate schedule, encoder/depth-estimator choices, and attention/mixing depths. Appendix G adds pseudocode. This substantially expands reproducibility information, although G.2's width slicing conflicts with its declared tensor layout.

R1.justification: Seven references are added for dataset provenance and implementation, including KITTI, KITTI-360, BEVDepth, AdamW, PyTorch, MobileStereoNet, and EfficientNet. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 1–5 remain largely verbatim. Changes include an author-name spelling correction, simplified Equation 6 exposition, an acknowledgement, and an organized A–G supplement preceding the references; the main narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The original figures and tables are retained. The supplement substantially expands visual presentation with five additional tables, a loss-sensitivity plot, four qualitative comparison figures, and two pseudocode listings, covering new controls, scene conditions, and implementation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's missing training recipe and limited controls for attributing gains to the proposed mechanisms. Appendices A–B improve implementation transparency, while D–E test simpler alternatives and challenging conditions; C exposes computational costs. These additions materially strengthen the paper's evidential support. Pseudocode indexing inconsistencies, unspecified scenario sample counts, and absent uncertainty estimates remain limitations.
